claims.text: Language models are highly sensitive to epistemic markers in prompts.
Language model accuracies vary by more than 80% depending on epistemic markers in prompts.
Expressions of high certainty result in a 7% decrease in accuracy compared to low certainty expressions.
Factive verbs hurt language model performance.
Markers of uncertainty in pretraining data are associated with answers on question-answering websites.
Markers of certainty in pretraining data are associated with questions on question-answering websites.

evidence.description: We find that LMs are highly sensitive to epistemic markers in prompts, with accuracies varying more than 80%.
expressions of high certainty result in a 7% decrease in accuracy as compared to low certainty expressions
these markers of uncertainty are associated with answers on question-answering websites
while markers of certainty are associated with questions

methodologies.name: Epistemic marker prompt injection
methodologies.description: Developed a typology of epistemic markers and injected 50 markers into prompts for question answering.
conditions: high certainty vs low certainty expressions

methodologies.name: Pretraining dataset analysis
methodologies.description: Analyzed associations between epistemic markers and question-answering website content in a popular pretraining dataset.

limitations.text: Behavior of LMs may be based on mimicking observed language use, rather than truly reflecting epistemic uncertainty.
